children.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to me: "When what does not exist does clinging not come to be? From the cessation of what is there the cessation of clinging?" Then, as I attended wisely—

children.text: evam eva upādānīyeṣu dharmeṣv anityānudarśino vibhavānudarśino virāgānudarśino nirodhānudarśinaḥ pratiniḥsargānudarśinas tṛṣṇā nirudhyate | tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ | pūrvavad yāvan nirodho bhavati |
children.translated_text: "Just so, for one who dwells perceiving impermanence, perceiving dissolution, perceiving dispassion, perceiving cessation, perceiving relinquishment in things subject to clinging—

children.text: atha te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan | abhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having rejoiced and given thanks, they departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: Sūtra 4

children.text: pūrvaṃ me bhikṣavo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim anabhisaṃbuddhasyaikākino rahasigatasyaivaṃ cetasi cetaḥparivitarka udapādi /
children.translated_text: "Before, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when I had not yet attained supreme, perfect awakening, while I was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind—

children.text: kṛcchraṃ batāyaṃ loka āpanno yad uta jāyate 'pi jīryate 'pi mriyate 'pi cyavate 'py upapadyate 'pi / atha ca punar ime satvā jarāmaraṇasyottare niḥsaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ na prajānanti /
children.translated_text: Alas, this world has fallen into difficulty — it is born, it ages, it dies, it passes away, and it is reborn. And yet these beings do not truly understand the escape beyond aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>).

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nu sati jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati / kiṃpratyayañ ca punar jarāmaraṇam / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / jātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati / jātipratyayañ ca punar jarāmaraṇam /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what exists does aging-and-death come to be? What is the condition for aging-and-death?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When birth (<s>jāti</s>) exists, aging-and-death comes to be. Birth is the condition for aging-and-death.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nu sati jātir bhavati / kiṃpratyayā ca punar jātiḥ /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what exists does birth come to be? What is the condition for birth?'

children.text: tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / bhave sati jātir bhavati / bhavapratyayā ca punar jātiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When existence (<s>bhava</s>) exists, birth comes to be. Existence is the condition for birth.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nu sati bhavo bhavati / kiṃpratyayaś ca punar bhavaḥ / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / upādāne sati bhavo bhavati / upādānapratyayaś ca punar bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what exists does existence come to be? What is the condition for existence?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When clinging (<s>upādāna</s>) exists, existence comes to be. Clinging is the condition for existence.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat | kasmin nu saty upādānaṃ bhavati | kiṃpratyayañ ca punar upādānam | tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi | upādānīyeṣu dharmeṣv āsvādānudarśino viharatas tṛṣṇā pravardhate | tṛsṇāpratyayam upādānam | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiḥ | jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati |
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what exists does clinging come to be? What is the condition for clinging?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: For one who dwells seeing enjoyment in things that can be clung to, craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) increases. Craving is the condition for clinging; clinging is the condition for existence; existence is the condition for birth; birth is the condition for aging-and-death — sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair arise. Thus there is the origination of this entire great mass of suffering.

children.text: evam eva upādānīyeṣu dharmeṣv āsvādānudarśino viharatas tṛṣā pravardhate tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiḥ | jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati |
children.translated_text: Just so — for one who dwells seeing enjoyment in things that can be clung to, craving increases. Craving is the condition for clinging; clinging is the condition for existence; existence is the condition for birth; birth is the condition for aging-and-death — sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair arise. Thus there is the origination of this entire great mass of suffering.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nv asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na bhavati / kasya nirodhāj jarāmaraṇanirodhaḥ / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / jātyām asatyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ na bhavati / jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇanirodha /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does aging-and-death not come to be? From the cessation of what comes the cessation of aging-and-death?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When birth does not exist, aging-and-death does not come to be. From the cessation of birth comes the cessation of aging-and-death.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nv asati jātir na bhavati / kasya nirodhāj jātinirodhaḥ / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udpādi bhave 'sati jātir na bhavati / bhavanirodhāj jātinirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does birth not come to be? From the cessation of what comes the cessation of birth?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When existence does not exist, birth does not come to be. From the cessation of existence comes the cessation of birth.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nv asati bhavo na bhavati / kasya nirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / upādāne 'sati bhavo na bhavati / upādānanirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does existence not come to be? From the cessation of what comes the cessation of existence?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: When clinging does not exist, existence does not come to be. From the cessation of clinging comes the cessation of existence.

children.text: tasya mamaitad abhavat / kasmin nv asaty upādānaṃ na bhavati / kasya nirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ / tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi / upādānīyeṣu dharmeṣv anityānudarśino vibhavānudarśino virāgānudarśino nirodhānudarśinaḥ pratiniḥsargānudarśinas tṛṣṇā nirudhyate | tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ | upādānanirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ | bhavanirodhāj jātinirodhaḥ | jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇanirodhaḥ | śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante / evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati |
children.translated_text: This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does clinging not come to be? From the cessation of what comes the cessation of clinging?' Through my proper mental attention, the realization of things as they truly are arose thus: For one who dwells seeing impermanence in things that can be clung to, seeing destruction, seeing dispassion, seeing cessation, seeing relinquishment — craving ceases. From the cessation of craving comes the cessation of clinging; from the cessation of clinging comes the cessation of existence; from the cessation of existence comes the cessation of birth; from the cessation of birth comes the cessation of aging-and-death — sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair cease. Thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering.

children.text: evam eva upādānīyeṣu dharmeṣv anityānudarśino vibhavānudarśino virāgānudarśino nirodhānudarśinaḥ pratiniḥsargānudarśinas tṛṣṇā nirudhyate | tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ | pūrvavad yāvan nirodho bhavati |
children.translated_text: Just so — for one who dwells seeing impermanence in things that can be clung to, seeing destruction, seeing dispassion, seeing cessation, seeing relinquishment — craving ceases. From the cessation of craving comes the cessation of clinging — as before, up to — cessation comes to be.

children.text: atha te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan | abhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One. Having rejoiced and approved, they departed from the presence of the Blessed One.

body.text: NidSa 5.20 tasya mamaitad abhavat | kasmin nv asati tṛṣṇā na bhavati | kasya nirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhaḥ | tasya mama yoniśo manasi kurvata evaṃ yathābhūtasyābhisamaya udapādi | vedanāyām asatyāṃ tṛṣṇā na bhavati | vedanānirodhāt ṭṣṇānirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: NidSa 5.20 This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) not exist? From the cessation of what is there cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>?' body.translated_text: NidSa 5.21 This thought occurred to me: 'When what does not exist does <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) not exist? From the cessation of what is there cessation of <s>vedanā</s>?' As I attended to this wisely, the realization of things as they truly are arose: when <s>sparśa</s> (contact) does not exist, <s>vedanā</s> does not exist; from the cessation of <s>sparśa</s>, cessation of <s>vedanā</s>.

body.text: NidSa 14.7 pratītyasamutpannā dharmāḥ katame | avidyā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sparśo vedanā tṛṣṇā upādānaṃ bhavo jātir jarāmaraṇaṃ | ima ucyante pratītyasamutpannā dharmāḥ |
body.translated_text: "What are dependently arisen phenomena? <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), <s>bhava</s> (becoming), <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death)—these are called dependently arisen phenomena."

body.text: NidSa 14.8 yataś ca śrutavatāryaśrāvakeṇa pratītyasamutpādaś ca pratītyasamutpannāś ca dharmā yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā sudṛṣṭā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: "Inasmuch as the learned noble disciple has well seen with right wisdom, as it truly is, both <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and dependently arisen phenomena—"

body.text: NidSa 14.9 sa na pūrvāntaṃ pratisarati | kin nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvani | aho svin nāham atīte 'dhvani | ko nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvani | kathaṃ nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvani |
body.translated_text: "He does not run back to the past: 'Was I in the past? Or was I not in the past? What was I in the past? How was I in the past?'"

body.translated_text: "Nor does he run forward to the future: 'Shall I be in the future? Or shall I not be in the future? What shall I be in the future? How shall I be in the future?'"

body.text: NidSa 14.11 adhyātmaṃ vākathaṃkathībhavati | kiṃ svid idam | kathaṃ svid idam | ke santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ | ayaṃ satvaḥ kuta āgataḥ | sa itaś cyutaḥ kutragāmī bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: "Nor does he have inner doubt: 'What is this? How is this? Being what, what shall we become? This being—from where has it come? Having departed from here, where will it go?'"

Sūtra 15: Emptiness
Among the <s>Kurus</s>, the preamble.
There the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>:

body.text: NidSa 15.3 dharmaṃ vo deśayiṣye ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ yāvat prakāśayiṣye | yad uta mahāśūnyatānāma dharmaparyāyas tac chṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye |
body.translated_text: "I shall teach you a <s>Dharma</s> that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end—I shall illuminate it. Namely, the discourse on <s>Mahāśūnyatā</s> (Great Emptiness). Listen to that, well and properly attend to it in your minds; I shall speak."

body.text: NidSa 15.4 mahāśūnyatādharmaparyāyāḥ katamāḥ | yad utāsmin satīdaṃ bhavaty asyotpādād idam utpadyate | yad utāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvat samudayo bhavati |
body.translated_text: "What is the discourse on <s>Mahāśūnyatā</s> (Great Emptiness)? Namely: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is: with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as condition, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)—up to: thus is the origination."

iti ya evaṃ vaded ayaṃ jarāmaraṇam asya vā jarāmaraṇam | yaś caivaṃ vadet taj jīvaṃ tac charīram anyaj jīvam anyac charīram | ubhayam etad ekam | vyañjanam atra nānā |
body.translated_text: "With <s>jāti</s> (birth) as condition, <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death). Therein, there may be questioners asking: 'Who undergoes old age and death? Whose is old age and death?' And one who would say: 'This is old age and death; it is his old age and death'; and one who would say: 'The life-principle is the same as the body'—"

body.text:
NidSa 15.5b taj jīvaṃ tac charīram iti dṛṣṭau satyāṃ brahmacaryavāso na bhavati | anyaj jīvam anyac charīram iti bhikṣavo dṛṣṭau satyāṃ brahmacaryavāso na bhavati |
ity etāv ubhāv antāv anupagamyāsti madhyamā pratipad āryā lokottarā yathābhūtā aviparītā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | yad uta jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam |
body.translated_text: NidSa 15.5b When the view 'the life-principle (<s>jīva</s>) is the same as the body' holds, the living of the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) does not obtain. When the view 'the life-principle is different from the body' holds, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the living of the holy life does not obtain. Without resorting to either of these two extremes, there is a middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>), noble, supramundane, according to reality, unerring — right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>): namely, that aging-and-death is conditioned by birth.

body.text: NidSa 15.6 evaṃ jātir bhava upādānaṃ tṛṣṇā vedanā sparśaḥ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ nāmarūpaṃ vijñānam |
body.translated_text: NidSa 15.6 Likewise, birth [is conditioned by] existence, existence by clinging, clinging by craving, craving by feeling, feeling by contact, contact by the six sense-bases, the six sense-bases by name-and-form, name-and-form by consciousness.

body.translated_text: NidSa 16.2 What is the beginning of dependent origination? Namely: 'When this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises.' body.translated_text: NidSa 16.16 What is death (<s>maraṇa</s>)?
